novelty_delta: Thirtieth behaviour. On its own the screen is only modestly novel next to finiteness_selection -- both read a verb-selected frame -- and I am recording that rather than overstating it. Two things make it non-duplicative. First, the design puts an intervening temporal adverbial between the verb and the read position, so the cue sits two tokens back and a carrying site cannot be reading the verb locally; finiteness_selection reads immediately off the verb. Second, and the actual reason to run it: the negation work just showed that two features in one domain can be near-orthogonal directions at the same site rather than one shared feature. Whether verb subcategorization is ONE direction or many is the same question in a different domain, and it cannot be asked without a second verb-frame behaviour.
